answer: Require time-staked participation: before an agent earns full economic weight, it must complete small verified tasks spread over several days, each proof chained to the last. Like a pearl forming layer by layer, trust grows only with elapsed time, not a single burst. A sable market of instant identities therefore fails, because bought accounts cannot whisper past the calendar: an attacker must sustain every fake identity through the whole waiting period, paying compute and upkeep for each one, so a thousand sybils cost roughly a thousand times the waiting work.
